general.temas: The summit between Russia, the United States and China dominates the front pages, alongside the war in Ukraine and its consequences. The launch of GTA VI, Russia’s warning to Wikimedia, the record sale of a Van Gogh painting and Segezha’s results also recur. Only Meduza highlights the International Court of Justice’s ruling on the genocide of the Rohingya in Myanmar.
general.motivo_crispacion: The war between Russia and Ukraine is the main source of heightened tension, with reports of attacks, civilian casualties and threats of retaliation following strikes on the Crimean Bridge. Komsomólskaya Pravda accuses Europe and Kyiv of trying to derail the summit, while Putin rejects ceasefire negotiations after the attacks on the bridge. The Russian prosecutor’s warning to Wikimedia adds another source of conflict. Diplomatic coverage and news about science, culture and video games partly offset that tension.

Kommersant.resumen:
- The APEC forum brings together the leaders of Russia, China and the United States; coverage also highlights Ukraine’s absence from their talks and Putin’s meeting with the Japanese prime minister.
- The European Commission proposes a €45 billion loan to cover part of Ukraine’s budget deficit.
- Segezha Group improves its quarterly OIBDA, while a trial in absentia begins in Moscow over an alleged 50 billion ruble bank fraud.
- Two candidates will challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency; Alexander Zverev faces a new lawsuit from his former partner.
- The front page includes the release of a film about Elizabeth Holmes, the record sale of a Van Gogh, a new novel and the impact of GTA 6 on internet traffic in Russia.
Kommersant.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “summit of the sensible,” “sensation” and “notoriously scandalous shadow financier” add emphasis and judgment.
Kommersant.sesgo: International coverage adopts a mainly Russian perspective, featuring views from Russian analysts and attention to Moscow’s role. The selection combines that focus with economic, sports and cultural news.

Rossíiskaya Gazeta.resumen:
- Oncologists explain a therapy that modifies a patient’s cells to fight leukemia.
- The Perm region receives an award for an infrastructure project.
- A woman was killed and her grandson injured in a drone attack in Bryansk, according to the regional governor.
- Russia’s prosecutor’s office warns Wikimedia that its activities could be declared undesirable; a possible Anthropic IPO could make its employees rich.
- Putin reports on talks with Xi Jinping and Donald Trump about the UN, nuclear weapons and security; the coverage also includes science, automobile and sports news.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative, although expressions such as “defeat leukemia” and the reference to employees who could become millionaires are intended to make an impact.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.sesgo: The selection gives space to Russian authorities and institutions, with news of their initiatives and statements, alongside prominent attention to Russia and China. An institutional approach predominates, although scientific, sports and economic topics also appear.

Komsomólskaya Pravda.resumen:
- The meeting of Putin, Xi and Trump dominates the front page, with analysis of their gestures, hierarchy and possible agreements.
- One headline accuses Europe and Kyiv of trying to derail the meeting; another reports Putin’s assurances about supplies to Crimea after an attack on the bridge.
- Lawmakers promise to investigate construction costs and housing prices.
- An expert explains the anticipation surrounding the launch of GTA VI.
- Several stories cover a gala, divorces, legal disputes and celebrity anecdotes.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.motivo_populismo: Headlines such as “terrorism did not prevail,” “Europe and Kyiv horrified” and “here is strength” rely on confrontation, drama and sensationalism, although there is no explicit appeal to the people against the elites.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.sesgo: The selection and wording portray Putin and the Russian position favorably, while attributing hostile actions to Europe and Kyiv. The front page combines that political approach with abundant entertainment and celebrity content.

Védomosti.resumen:
- The meeting of Putin, Trump and Xi in Shenzhen dominates coverage, with statements and reactions to the encounter.
- The front page addresses the prospects for peace and the final declaration of the APEC summit.
- The Duma passed the draft federal budget for 2027–2029 on its second reading.
- Rosneft placed fifth in a global ranking and Segezha reported an improvement in its OIBDA.
- Other stories cover the resignation of Mongolia’s president, Russian fashion and luxury housing in Moscow.
Védomosti.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative, although expressions such as “first in history” and “a page in the history of diplomacy” emphasize the exceptional nature of the meeting.
Védomosti.sesgo: The selection prioritizes Russian diplomatic activity and Putin’s statements, alongside economic news about Russian companies. It also includes foreign media perspectives on the prospects for peace.

Meduza.resumen:
- Russia attacked Kyiv with drones after a summit with the United States and China; one person was reported killed and others injured.
- Putin refused to agree to a ceasefire after the attacks on the Crimean Bridge, threatened a response and proposed talks in Moscow with European representatives.
- The front page examines Sergei Kiriyenko’s increased public presence and Russia’s ability to respond to attacks on the bridge.
- Russia’s prosecutor’s office warned Wikimedia that it could declare its activities undesirable; former Deputy Defense Minister Ruslan Tsalikov was sentenced to ten years in prison.
- Also highlighted are the International Court of Justice ruling against Myanmar, the launch of GTA VI and the record sale of a Van Gogh work.
Meduza.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “suspiciously often” and the contrast between the summit and the attack on Kyiv add drama; there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Meduza.sesgo: The selection and wording show a critical approach to the Russian authorities, particularly in coverage of the war and Kiriyenko. They also report Putin’s statements on the war and negotiations.

opiniones.comunista:
The great-power summit cannot be judged by its statements alone: peace must also be judged by the lives of those who suffer through war. Meduza reports one person killed and others injured in Kyiv after a Russian attack; in Bryansk, according to regional authorities, a Ukrainian attack killed a woman and injured her grandson. I support a ceasefire and negotiations that protect civilians, not a policy of retaliation.

Meanwhile, the Duma has passed the budget on its second reading, and housing prices are being debated. For me, the question is whom public resources serve. I want sufficient public healthcare and housing, funded progressively, and collective ownership under democratic control wherever big capital turns basic needs into opportunities for profit. The working class must not pay for crises and wars while others accumulate wealth.
opiniones.anarquista:
While the leaders of Russia, China and the United States talk about security in Shenzhen, news reports describe a Russian drone attack on Kyiv, with people killed and injured, and another attributed to Ukrainian forces in Bryansk, where a woman was killed and her grandson injured. I do not confuse diplomacy with peace: I doubt that states, which hold the power to wage war, can by themselves guarantee a just peace. Those who suffer from their decisions must have a voice and a real ability to organize.

I am also concerned about the Russian prosecutor’s warning to the Wikimedia Foundation. Shared knowledge should not depend on the state’s permission. In place of the authority of governments and parties, I support communities able to manage their resources, sustain themselves through mutual aid and preserve individual and collective freedom.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned that Russia’s prosecutor’s office has warned Wikimedia that its activities could be declared undesirable. A free society does not need the state to decide for its citizens which sources they may consult. If information is wrong, it must be possible to discuss and correct it, not silence it. Freedom of expression also requires individual responsibility: reading critically, checking information against other sources and admitting one’s own mistakes.

The passage of the federal budget on its second reading leads me to another question: how much room will be left for people to decide what to do with the fruits of their labor? I support low taxes, scrutiny of spending and a state limited to essential functions. Not because collective problems do not matter, but because concentrating resources and decisions in government does not guarantee that they will be solved. Private enterprise and competition deserve room to offer alternatives.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I do not confuse a photograph of three great powers with a guarantee of security. The meeting in Shenzhen may open diplomatic channels, but Russia must defend its interests without surrendering its sovereignty to agreements among elites far removed from the consequences of their decisions.

The death of a woman in Bryansk and the victims of the Russian attack on Kyiv are reminders that security requires protecting civilians, not just displaying strength. It also requires reliable infrastructure: after the attacks on the Crimean Bridge, supplies cannot depend on improvised promises.

And national strength begins at home. The corruption conviction of a former senior defense official shows why patriotism must include accountability. A secure nation needs institutions of integrity, its own industry and families able to look to the future with confidence.
opiniones.centro:
I welcome the fact that Russia, the United States and China are talking about nuclear security: even adversaries must keep diplomatic channels open. But let us not confuse a summit with peace. Accounts differ on whether Ukraine was discussed, while Meduza reports a Russian drone attack on Kyiv and Rossíiskaya Gazeta attributes the death of a civilian woman in Bryansk to a Ukrainian attack. I support negotiations that include Ukraine and Europe, with verifiable guarantees and protection for civilians.

I am also concerned about the Russian prosecutor’s warning to Wikimedia. A society needs open information and the ability to correct errors, not threats that restrict access to knowledge. The proposed European loan to Ukraine could help sustain its services, but it must be accompanied by budget transparency and parliamentary oversight: solidarity lasts longer when it is accountable.
